<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S6.SS5" title="In 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">6.5 </span>Does experience accumulate across agents?</span></a></li>
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S6.SS6" title="In 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">6.6 </span>How does EvolveNet compare with centralized evolution?</span></a></li>
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S6.SS7" title="In 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">6.7 </span>Does any of this depend on the model?</span></a></li>
<li class="ltx_tocentry ltx_tocentry_subsection"><a href="#S6.SS8" title="In 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">6.8 </span>Scaling evolutionary search through parallel trajectories</span></a></li>

</ol></li>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Jun Nie
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">

</span></span></span></span>

Code: <a href="https://github.com/junnie00/EvolveNet" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/junnie00/EvolveNet</a>
</span></span></span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">

</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">

Code: <a href="https://github.com/junnie00/EvolveNet" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/junnie00/EvolveNet</a>

<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">

</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">

</span></span></span></span>

</span></span>

Hong Kong Baptist University

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">The capabilities of an LLM agent depend not only on its model but on the <em id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">harness</em>:
the executable program that constructs context, invokes tools, verifies results, and recovers from
failure. Recent work shows that evolving the harness yields persistent improvements without updating
model weights. Existing approaches, however, assume that all execution experience can be routed
to a single optimizer, which evolves one harness along a sequential trajectory. Real agent ecosystems violate that assumption: users, organizations, and
environments generate isolated streams of experience that cannot be pooled, so the experience most worth
learning from is exactly the experience that cannot be directly centralized. We introduce <em id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">EvolveNet</em>, a paradigm of collaborative harness evolution that moves experience
extraction to the data. A shared harness is broadcast to data-local agent deployments, each of which
evolves it on its own workload. Only the resulting program adaptations are composed into an updated shared
harness and redistributed, so that every participating agent inherits operational experience discovered by
the others. By shifting the aggregation boundary from raw workloads to learned
adaptations, EvolveNet keeps workloads local and allows multiple evolutionary searches to
proceed concurrently with reduced serial depth. Because independently modified programs cannot be averaged like model
parameters and may conflict when composed, EvolveNet introduces scope-typed, evidence-guided program
aggregation. Across five settings spanning text-to-SQL, data-science coding, competitive programming, software
engineering, and agentic workflows, EvolveNet improves the shared harness in all five, with the largest
gains under heterogeneous workloads, and ablations attribute the improvement to composition of
adaptations from different agents rather than to selecting among them.</p>
  
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Large language model agents are not defined by the model alone. Their behavior also depends critically on
the surrounding <em id="S1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">harness</em>: the executable program that constructs context, invokes models and tools,
verifies intermediate results, and determines how the system responds to failure. Two agents built on the
same frozen model can exhibit substantially different capabilities simply because their harnesses implement
different reasoning procedures, tool-use policies, and recovery mechanisms. This observation has motivated
a growing line of work on improving the program around the model, including prompt optimization, workflow
search, and direct evolution of agent source code
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fernando et al. 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al. 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. 2025a</a>)</cite>. More recent studies make the
harness itself the persistent state of adaptation, showing that an agent can acquire durable behavioral
improvements without modifying its underlying model weights
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">He et al. 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al. 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nie et al. 2026</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Existing harness-evolution methods, however, largely follow a centralized paradigm.
Workloads, execution traces, and behavioral feedback must first be made available to a
single optimizer, which extracts useful experience from them and evolves one harness
along a largely sequential trajectory. This paradigm is natural when all experience is
centrally accessible, but it couples the exploitation of distributed experience to workload
centralization. Moreover, as additional workloads are introduced, their adaptations must
be explored through the same evolving program, limiting both the breadth of search and
the serial efficiency of harness evolution.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Real agent deployments are naturally distributed across users, organizations, databases,
repositories, and tool environments. This suggests reversing the order in which experience
is extracted and aggregated. Rather than first pooling the workloads that contain useful
experience and then learning from them centrally, each deployment can first translate its
local executions and failures into an improved harness, after which the resulting program
adaptations can be aggregated. In other words, the object crossing the system boundary
changes from experience-bearing workloads to executable representations of the experience
learned from them.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">This shift creates a different paradigm for agent self-evolution. Local workloads can remain
where they are generated, while multiple deployments explore distinct evolutionary trajectories
concurrently. Their discoveries can then be accumulated in a shared harness and redistributed,
so that each client begins the next round from adaptations the others discovered.
Parallel local evolution does not reduce the total amount of search, but it reduces its serial
depth: the client phase is governed by the slowest concurrent branch rather than by the sum
of all local searches.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce <span id="S1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EvolveNet</span> to realize this paradigm.
EvolveNet begins each round from a common shared harness, broadcasts it to multiple data-local
clients, and evolves it independently on their local workloads. Each client thereby extracts
local operational experience into a specialist program. The server then integrates the
returned adaptations into an updated shared harness and redistributes it as the shared
starting point for the next round. EvolveNet therefore replaces the conventional
<em id="S1.p5.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">aggregate-data-then-evolve</em> pipeline with an
<em id="S1.p5.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">evolve-locally-then-aggregate</em> cycle, turning distributed local search into cumulative
progress in one executable agent system.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">The key obstacle is aggregation, and it is not the one federated optimization solves: the object being
combined is neither a parameter vector nor a collection of modules with a predefined
composition rule, but interacting executable programs whose semantics appear only when they run. In parameter-space aggregation, locally learned
information is encoded in vectors that can be combined through arithmetic operations such
as weighted averaging. Harness adaptations are source-program modifications: they have no
meaningful arithmetic average, and individually beneficial edits may become redundant,
contradictory, or invalid when composed. One client may strengthen a verification rule that
another removes; two clients may alter the same control path for different local reasons; and
a locally useful prompt edit may damage behavior elsewhere. Collaborative harness evolution
therefore depends not merely on communication, but on determining which adaptations are
transferable, how local specialization should be preserved, and whether their composition
retains existing capabilities.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">EvolveNet addresses this challenge through evidence-guided, scope-typed program aggregation.
All clients branch from the same broadcast harness, allowing the server to reason over their
program deltas relative to a common base. Each delta is accompanied by measured behavioral
changes, enabling the server to integrate complementary mechanisms while distinguishing
globally transferable behavior from adaptations that should remain domain-conditioned.
Candidate merges are behaviorally validated before they become the next shared harness.
Clients are encouraged to specialize in their own workload slices so that parallel searches
produce complementary rather than redundant adaptations.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p8.1" class="ltx_p">Rounds therefore form a bidirectional adaptation loop: local specialists and the shared harness
shape one another: each specialist is evolved from the current shared program, while the next
shared program is composed from the adaptations those specialists discover. Collaboration here is
mediated by an artifact rather than interactive — clients neither communicate nor coordinate within
a round; experience found by one becomes available to the others only through the redistributed
harness.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">Evaluating the aggregation operator requires separating its contribution from the substantial
stochasticity and path dependence of local harness evolution. We therefore introduce a paired
evaluation protocol in which competing aggregation rules are applied to identical snapshots
of locally evolved client programs. This isolates differences caused by aggregation from
differences in the client populations received by each rule.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p10" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">Across five settings spanning text-to-SQL, data-science coding, competitive programming,
software engineering, and agentic workflows, EvolveNet improves the shared harness in every
setting, with its largest gains when deployments hold disjoint forms of expertise.
On the most heterogeneous setting, paired ablations attribute these gains to composing client
adaptations rather than selecting or routing among complete specialists: the merged harness retains
adaptations discovered by different clients and combines them into behavior that no single client
produced. Our
contributions are as follows:</p>
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce <span id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">collaborative harness evolution</span>, a paradigm that moves
experience extraction from a centralized optimizer to data-local agent deployments and aggregates
the resulting executable adaptations rather than the workloads that produced them.
This enables distributed experience to accumulate in a shared harness while local
evolutionary searches proceed concurrently (Sec. <a href="#S4" title="4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We identify <span id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">program aggregation</span> as the central technical challenge of this
paradigm and develop an evidence-guided, scope-typed aggregation operator that
integrates harness deltas relative to a common base, promotes transferable mechanisms
to global behavior, and preserves domain-specific adaptations under conditional scopes
(Sec. <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Evidence-guided, scope-typed program aggregation ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We establish an evaluation protocol that separates aggregation quality from the
stochasticity of local evolution, and apply it across five settings. Complementary
adaptations discovered by different clients accumulate in one shared harness,
with the largest gains under heterogeneous workloads, while parallel local
evolution reduces the serial depth of search and requires only one server-side
aggregation session per round (Secs. <a href="#S6.SS2" title="6.2 Main results ‣ 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.2</span></a>–<a href="#S6.SS8" title="6.8 Scaling evolutionary search through parallel trajectories ‣ 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.8</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related Work</h2>

<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Optimizing the program around a frozen model.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A substantial body of work improves LLM systems
by optimizing the structures that surround the model rather than its weights. Prompt optimization searches
for instructions through iterative refinement, evolutionary search, or by treating the LLM itself as an
optimizer <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhou et al. 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fernando et al. 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al. 2024</a>)</cite>; DSPy optimizes
multi-stage pipelines <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Khattab et al. 2024</a>)</cite>; and automated agent design searches over tool-use workflows
and control structures <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al. 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. 2025b</a>)</cite>. A closely related line treats executable programs
themselves as the object of improvement — STOP recursively improves code-generating programs
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zelikman et al. 2023</a>)</cite>, FunSearch pairs language models with program evaluation
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Romera-Paredes et al. 2024</a>)</cite>, the Darwin Gödel Machine explores open-ended self-modification
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. 2025a</a>)</cite>, and MOSS rewrites an agent’s own source <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cai et al. 2026</a>)</cite> — and, most recently,
makes the agent <em id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">harness</em> the persistent state of adaptation, optimizing the control program that
organizes model calls, tools, feedback and recovery
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">He et al. 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lee et al. 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al. 2026</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nie et al. 2026</a>)</cite>. These methods are typically instantiated as a single
optimization process over centrally accessible experience, producing one evolutionary trajectory. They
study how <em id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">one</em> agent improves; EvolveNet studies how improvements discovered by <em id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">many</em> agents
accumulate in a shared evolving artifact. EvolveNet asks what changes
when that experience is partitioned across deployments and cannot be centralized.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Collaborative improvement through shared artifacts.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A line of work enables distributed
agents to collaborate by exchanging learned artifacts rather than the data that produced them. FederatedSkill shares
semantic skill diffs that a server folds into a shared skill library <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. 2026</a>)</cite>,
Fed-SE aggregates parameter-efficient adapter updates across environments <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al. 2025</a>)</cite>, and
Federation over Text distills clients’ reasoning traces into a shared textual insight library
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yao et al. 2026</a>)</cite>. All inherit the broadcast–optimize–aggregate–redistribute schedule of
decentralized model training, from FedAvg <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">McMahan et al. 2017</a>)</cite> through methods addressing instability
and statistical heterogeneity <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al. 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Karimireddy et al. 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Reddi et al. 2021</a>)</cite>. EvolveNet shares the high-level communication pattern of these systems, but the object it optimizes and
the aggregation problem that object induces are of a different kind. Each of them assumes client updates
can be expressed in a predefined aggregation space — a weight tensor, an adapter, a list of skills, a
set of textual insights — in which combination is well defined a priori. Here the aggregation space is
itself a programming language, and whether two contributions combine is a fact about execution rather
than a property of the representation. What it circulates is the
<em id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">executable control program</em> itself, and targets a single scope-conditioned shared artifact rather than a library of
independent patches, insights, or adapter weights. This changes what aggregation is: skill patches compose
by insertion and insights by concatenation, whereas program edits interact through control flow, prompts,
tool calls, and runtime state, so the server cannot rely on averaging, numerical distance, or any
gradient-based notion of agreement, and must instead reason about program behavior.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">A different sense of collaboration appears at inference time, where agents exchange messages, debate, or
delegate subtasks in order to answer one query <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Du et al. 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wu et al. 2023</a>)</cite>. EvolveNet collaborates
across adaptation rounds instead: its clients evolve independently within a round and never exchange
messages, and their contributions meet only in a persistent shared harness that accumulates and
redistributes them.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Model merging.</h4>

<div id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Model merging consolidates independently acquired capabilities relative to a
common base without retraining on the union of their data. Task Arithmetic composes fine-tuned models as
parameter displacements <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ilharco et al. 2023</a>)</cite>, TIES-Merging reduces interference by removing
weak updates and resolving sign conflicts <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yadav et al. 2023</a>)</cite>, and DARE sparsifies and rescales deltas
before merging <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yu et al. 2024</a>)</cite>. EvolveNet shares the goal of combining capabilities relative to a shared
base while managing interference, but the aggregation spaces differ fundamentally: neural checkpoints
admit coordinate-wise arithmetic, whereas source-code edits have no intrinsic magnitude, direction, or
element-wise correspondence, and syntactically valid edits can interact in ways not inferable from the
edits alone. EvolveNet therefore uses execution-derived behavioral evidence both to guide integration and to
validate it, and aims not merely to select among complete client programs but to preserve and combine the
transferable adaptations distributed across them.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Preliminaries</h2>

<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Harness.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be a frozen LLM. A harness <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is an executable program that, given an input
<math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, may call <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> any number of times, execute tools, inspect results, and return an answer <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x)</annotation></semantics></math>. The
space <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math> of harnesses is the space of programs satisfying two invariants (Sec. <a href="#S5" title="5 Experimental Setup ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>):
the model is never changed, and gold labels are never read at inference.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Our local-evolution loop instantiates the trace-driven harness evolution of TTHE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Nie et al. 2026</a>)</cite>,
with an LLM proposer that reads execution traces and edits the harness source.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Distributed setting.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We consider <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> agent deployments that are <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">data-local</em>: each runs
where its workload is generated, and evolution happens there rather than at a central site. We refer to
them throughout the protocol as <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">clients</em>. Client <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> holds a workload <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> that cannot be pooled with the others.
Client <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> can execute a harness on <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, observe traces, and grade outcomes on its own data. Raw workloads and execution
records stay local; what crosses the boundary is program text, its delta against the common base, and
per-item behavioral verdicts.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Objective.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We seek a single shared harness <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> maximizing expected accuracy on a target
workload <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{target}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>target</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{target}}</annotation></semantics></math>, using only local evolution at the clients and aggregation at the
server. Only the client mixture is accessible during evolution; the target may also contain related domains
held by no client, as one of our evaluation domains does.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2608.04968v1/ppl.png" id="S3.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" width="548" height="309" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span><span id="S3.F1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Left:</span> conventional harness evolution is sequential. One optimizer consumes incoming
batches in order and each harness must be produced before the next can be explored, so a <math id="S3.F1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>-stage search
has serial depth <math id="S3.F1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> and follows a single trajectory. <span id="S3.F1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Right:</span> EvolveNet broadcasts the shared harness
<math id="S3.F1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S3.F1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> clients, which evolve it in parallel on the workloads held at each, into specialists
<math id="S3.F1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{k}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{k}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>. The server aggregates the returned programs rather than the workloads behind them, adopting a
mechanism globally when its supporting evidence spans domains and conditioning it on its home domain
otherwise, and commits the result as <math id="S3.F1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(t+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(t+1)}</annotation></semantics></math> only if it passes the per-item acceptance test
(Sec. <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Behavioral commitment and rollback ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>). The dashed edge closes the loop: the committed harness is redistributed, so each
client’s next round of evolution starts from what the whole collaboration has learned, not from its own
previous program.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Method: EvolveNet</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> denote a frozen language model and let a harness <math id="S4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h\in\mathcal{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h\in\mathcal{H}</annotation></semantics></math> be the executable program
that organizes calls to <math id="S4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, invokes tools, constructs context, verifies intermediate results, and handles
failures. We consider <math id="S4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> clients, where client <math id="S4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> holds a local workload <math id="S4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{k}^{\mathrm{tr}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>tr</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{k}^{\mathrm{tr}}</annotation></semantics></math> drawn from
deployment domain <math id="S4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>. Raw workloads remain at their respective clients. Our objective is to construct a
single shared harness that accumulates useful adaptations discovered across these domains:</p>
<table id="S4.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{\star}=\arg\max_{h\in\mathcal{H}}\mathbb{E}_{z\sim\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{target}}}\left[s(h;z)\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>arg</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi></mrow></munder></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>target</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{\star}=\arg\max_{h\in\mathcal{H}}\mathbb{E}_{z\sim\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{target}}}\left[s(h;z)\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{target}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>target</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{target}}</annotation></semantics></math> is the deployment distribution the shared harness must serve and <math id="S4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>
is a task-specific evaluation function. During evolution EvolveNet has access only to the client mixture
<math id="S4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{client}}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\pi_{k}\mathcal{P}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>client</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{client}}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\pi_{k}\mathcal{P}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is client <math id="S4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>’s
deployment distribution and <math id="S4.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> its mixture weight; <math id="S4.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{client}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>client</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{client}}</annotation></semantics></math> may cover only
part of <math id="S4.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{target}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>target</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{target}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and our evaluation includes a domain held by no client
(Table <a href="#S6.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 6.2 Main results ‣ 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>). The model <math id="S4.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> remains fixed throughout;
all adaptation occurs in the harness.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>From centralized evolution to collaborative harness evolution</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Conventional harness evolution follows an <em id="S4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">aggregate-workloads-then-evolve</em> paradigm. Workloads,
execution traces, and behavioral feedback are first made available to a centralized optimizer, which
extracts useful experience from them and updates one harness along a single evolutionary trajectory. In
conceptual form,</p>
<table id="S4.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\underbrace{\operatorname{Pool}\left(D_{1}^{\mathrm{tr}},\ldots,D_{K}^{\mathrm{tr}}\right)\;\longrightarrow\;\operatorname{Evolve}}_{\text{centralized harness evolution}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><munder><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mrow><mi>Pool</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>tr</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>K</mi><mi>tr</mi></msubsup><mo rspace="0.280em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em" stretchy="false">⟶</mo><mi>Evolve</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><mtext>centralized harness evolution</mtext></munder><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\underbrace{\operatorname{Pool}\left(D_{1}^{\mathrm{tr}},\ldots,D_{K}^{\mathrm{tr}}\right)\;\longrightarrow\;\operatorname{Evolve}}_{\text{centralized harness evolution}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">This design couples experience extraction to workload centralization. It also places all adaptation
pressure on one evolving program: additional workloads can enlarge the available experience, but their
adaptations must still be discovered through the same central search process.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">EvolveNet reverses this order (Fig. <a href="#S3.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ Objective. ‣ 3 Preliminaries ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). Each client first extracts operational experience from its own workload by
evolving the shared harness locally. The server then aggregates the resulting <em id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">program adaptations</em>,
rather than the workloads that produced them:</p>
<table id="S4.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\underbrace{\operatorname{Evolve}_{1:K}\left(h^{(t)},D_{1:K}^{\mathrm{tr}}\right)\;\longrightarrow\;\operatorname{Aggregate}\left(\Delta_{1:K}^{(t)}\right)}_{\text{collaborative harness evolution}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><munder accentunder="true"><mrow><mi>Evolve</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></msub><mo>(</mo><mi>h</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>tr</mi></msup><mo rspace="0.280em">)</mo><mo rspace="0.558em" stretchy="false">⟶</mo><mi>Aggregate</mi><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true">⏟</mo></munder><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>collaborative harness evolution</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\underbrace{\operatorname{Evolve}_{1:K}\left(h^{(t)},D_{1:K}^{\mathrm{tr}}\right)\;\longrightarrow\;\operatorname{Aggregate}\left(\Delta_{1:K}^{(t)}\right)}_{\text{collaborative harness evolution}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">At round <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, all clients receive the same shared harness <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>. Client <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> applies a local evolution
operator <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}</annotation></semantics></math> to obtain</p>
<table id="S4.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{k}^{(t)}=\mathcal{E}\left(h^{(t)},D_{k}^{\mathrm{tr}}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>tr</mi></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{k}^{(t)}=\mathcal{E}\left(h^{(t)},D_{k}^{\mathrm{tr}}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">The local proposer is encouraged to specialize in the recurring structures and failure modes of domain
<math id="S4.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, rather than reproduce a generic solution already available to all clients. The broadcast harness is
always retained in the local candidate pool. Therefore, if <math id="S4.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the client-side selection score,</p>
<table id="S4.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{k}\!\left(h_{k}^{(t)}\right)\geq S_{k}\!\left(h^{(t)}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{k}\!\left(h_{k}^{(t)}\right)\geq S_{k}\!\left(h^{(t)}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.4" class="ltx_p">up to the resolution of the client evaluator. Local specialization thus produces candidate capabilities
without forcing a client to return a program that is measurably worse than the shared starting point on
its own workload.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The server integrates the returned adaptations into a candidate shared harness,</p>
<table id="S4.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}=\mathcal{A}\left(h^{(t)},h_{1}^{(t)},\ldots,h_{K}^{(t)}\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>K</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}=\mathcal{A}\left(h^{(t)},h_{1}^{(t)},\ldots,h_{K}^{(t)}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">which, after behavioral validation, is redistributed as the starting point for the next round. This
produces a recurring <math id="S4.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textsc{specialize}\rightarrow\textsc{aggregate}\rightarrow\textsc{redistribute}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">specialize</mtext><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">aggregate</mtext><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">redistribute</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textsc{specialize}\rightarrow\textsc{aggregate}\rightarrow\textsc{redistribute}</annotation></semantics></math>
cycle. Adaptations discovered locally are therefore not terminal client-specific outcomes: once integrated
into the shared harness, they become part of the initial state from which all clients evolve in the
following round. This is the sense in which the local specialists and the shared harness co-evolve — each
specialist is evolved from the current shared program, while the next shared program is assembled from the
adaptations those specialists produce. Clients do not interact directly within a round; their coupling
occurs through the shared executable artifact across rounds.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">This change in paradigm also alters the serial structure of search. Let <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{k}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{k}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> be the latency of the
local search conducted by client <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> in round <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\mathcal{A}}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\mathcal{A}}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S4.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\mathrm{val}}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>val</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\mathrm{val}}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> denote aggregation and validation latencies. Executing the same <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> local
searches serially would require
<math id="S4.SS1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\mathrm{serial}}^{(t)}=\sum_{k}C_{k}^{(t)}+C_{\mathcal{A}}^{(t)}+C_{\mathrm{val}}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>serial</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>val</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\mathrm{serial}}^{(t)}=\sum_{k}C_{k}^{(t)}+C_{\mathcal{A}}^{(t)}+C_{\mathrm{val}}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>,
whereas the parallel client phase in EvolveNet has serial depth</p>
<table id="S4.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\mathrm{EvolveNet}}^{(t)}=\max_{k}C_{k}^{(t)}+C_{\mathcal{A}}^{(t)}+C_{\mathrm{val}}^{(t)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>EvolveNet</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mi>k</mi></munder><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>val</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\mathrm{EvolveNet}}^{(t)}=\max_{k}C_{k}^{(t)}+C_{\mathcal{A}}^{(t)}+C_{\mathrm{val}}^{(t)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">EvolveNet does not eliminate the computational cost of local search; it makes multiple evolutionary
trajectories available at a serial depth governed by the slowest client rather than by their sum.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>The program-aggregation challenge</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The paradigm above depends on an aggregation operation that has no direct counterpart in parameter-space
aggregation. Model updates inhabit a common vector space and can be combined by coordinate-wise
arithmetic, as in weight averaging <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">McMahan et al. 2017</a>)</cite>. Source programs do not. There is no meaningful average of two Python harnesses, and
independently useful modifications need not remain useful when placed in the same executable system.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Program aggregation must address three coupled difficulties. First, it must establish <em id="S4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">attribution</em>:
a returned program may contain several interacting edits, and the server must determine which behavioral
changes are associated with that client variant. Second, it must manage <em id="S4.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">interference</em>: two
adaptations may be redundant, may alter the same control path in incompatible ways, or may encode
different assumptions about the deployment domain. Third, it must control <em id="S4.SS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">regression</em>: syntactically
valid and individually successful edits may still break capabilities already present in the shared harness
after composition.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">EvolveNet addresses these difficulties through four connected principles: all clients are compared against a
common program base; source-level changes are accompanied by measured behavioral evidence; candidate
mechanisms are assigned an explicit deployment scope before composition; and the composed program is
evaluated behaviorally before it replaces the current shared harness.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Evidence-guided, scope-typed program aggregation</h3>

<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Common-base program deltas.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Because every client starts from the same <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>, its
contribution can be represented as</p>
<table id="S4.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{k}^{(t)}=\operatorname{diff}\left(h^{(t)},h_{k}^{(t)}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>diff</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{k}^{(t)}=\operatorname{diff}\left(h^{(t)},h_{k}^{(t)}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The server edits a byte-for-byte copy of <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> rather than synthesizing a new program from <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>
complete files. This common-base representation serves two purposes. It makes client contributions
directly comparable, since each delta expresses what changed relative to the same behavioral state, and it
limits uncontrolled artifact growth caused by concatenating entire client programs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The aggregator decomposes each delta into candidate <em id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">mechanisms</em>. A mechanism is a semantically
coherent adaptation that implements a recognizable behavior — for example, an execution-retry rule, a
schema probe, an output-format constraint, or a repository-specific repair procedure. A mechanism need not
correspond exactly to one syntactic diff hunk: several nearby edits may jointly implement one behavior.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Behavioral evidence.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Source code alone does not reveal whether a client modification is
useful. While selecting its local program, client <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> therefore compares <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{k}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{k}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> with the broadcast
harness on its own workload and reports the resulting behavioral changes. Let <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{i}(h)\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{i}(h)\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> denote
the task evaluator’s verdict for item <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. We define</p>
<table id="S4.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.E9"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle F_{k}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle F_{k}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E9.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle=\left\{i\in D_{k}^{\mathrm{tr}}:v_{i}\!\left(h^{(t)}\right)=0,\,v_{i}\!\left(h_{k}^{(t)}\right)=1\right\}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>tr</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\left\{i\in D_{k}^{\mathrm{tr}}:v_{i}\!\left(h^{(t)}\right)=0,\,v_{i}\!\left(h_{k}^{(t)}\right)=1\right\},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S4.E10"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle B_{k}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle B_{k}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E10.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle=\left\{i\in D_{k}^{\mathrm{tr}}:v_{i}\!\left(h^{(t)}\right)=1,\,v_{i}\!\left(h_{k}^{(t)}\right)=0\right\}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>tr</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\left\{i\in D_{k}^{\mathrm{tr}}:v_{i}\!\left(h^{(t)}\right)=1,\,v_{i}\!\left(h_{k}^{(t)}\right)=0\right\},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">and attach <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{k}^{(t)}=(F_{k}^{(t)},B_{k}^{(t)})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{k}^{(t)}=(F_{k}^{(t)},B_{k}^{(t)})</annotation></semantics></math> to the corresponding program delta. The evidence records
which capabilities were newly acquired and which were lost relative to the common base. It does not by
itself establish a causal mapping from each item to a particular line of code; rather, it constrains the
aggregator’s interpretation of the delta with observed behavior. The aggregation operator can now be
written more precisely as</p>
<table id="S4.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}=\mathcal{A}\left(h^{(t)},\left\{\left(\Delta_{k}^{(t)},e_{k}^{(t)}\right)\right\}_{k=1}^{K}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}=\mathcal{A}\left(h^{(t)},\left\{\left(\Delta_{k}^{(t)},e_{k}^{(t)}\right)\right\}_{k=1}^{K}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The adoption problem.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Aggregation is not a free-form rewrite. Decomposing the <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> deltas
yields a candidate set <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}=\{m_{1},\dots,m_{n}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}=\{m_{1},\dots,m_{n}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, each <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> carrying the evidence of the client
it came from. An <em id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">adoption</em> is a pair <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(S,\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(S,\tau)</annotation></semantics></math>: a subset <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\subseteq\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\subseteq\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> to incorporate
and a scope assignment <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> for its members, which together determine one composed program
<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(S,\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(S,\tau)</annotation></semantics></math>. Writing <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Fix}(S,\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Fix</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Fix}(S,\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Brk}(S,\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Brk</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Brk}(S,\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> for the items of the server’s
validation slice <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D^{\mathrm{val}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>D</mi><mi>val</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D^{\mathrm{val}}</annotation></semantics></math> that <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(S,\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(S,\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> newly solves and newly fails relative to <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>,
the server seeks</p>
<table id="S4.E12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\max_{S\subseteq\mathcal{M},\;\tau}\;\left|\mathrm{Fix}(S,\tau)\right|\quad\text{subject to}\quad\left|\mathrm{Brk}(S,\tau)\right|\leq\left|\mathrm{Fix}(S,\tau)\right|." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⊆</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.447em">,</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.280em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>Fix</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mtext>subject to</mtext><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>Brk</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mi>Fix</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max_{S\subseteq\mathcal{M},\;\tau}\;\left|\mathrm{Fix}(S,\tau)\right|\quad\text{subject to}\quad\left|\mathrm{Brk}(S,\tau)\right|\leq\left|\mathrm{Fix}(S,\tau)\right|.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">This is the aggregation problem in program space, and it is not solvable by search: the objective and the
constraint are defined by <em id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">executing</em> <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(S,\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(S,\tau)</annotation></semantics></math>, so each of the <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2^{|\mathcal{M}|}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{|\mathcal{M}|}</annotation></semantics></math> subsets and
their scope assignments would cost a full evaluation pass, and the mechanisms interact, so the objective
is neither separable nor monotone in <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math>. EvolveNet therefore splits Eq. <a href="#S4.E12" title="In The adoption problem. ‣ 4.3 Evidence-guided, scope-typed program aggregation ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> into a proposal
step and an exact feasibility check. The scope-typed aggregator (Sec. <a href="#S4.SS3" title="4.3 Evidence-guided, scope-typed program aggregation ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>) proposes one
<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(S,\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(S,\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> in a single pass by reasoning over the attached evidence rather than by enumeration; the
acceptance gate (Sec. <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Behavioral commitment and rollback ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>) then evaluates the realized program and enforces the constraint
exactly, rejecting the proposal when it fails. What the aggregator supplies is a heuristic for
