<em id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">which</em> mechanisms to adopt and <em id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.2.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">where</em> they should apply; what the gate supplies is the
guarantee that an adopted proposal actually satisfies Eq. <a href="#S4.E12" title="In The adoption problem. ‣ 4.3 Evidence-guided, scope-typed program aggregation ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Scope-typed composition.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The central decision is not simply whether to accept or reject a
mechanism, but <em id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">where</em> that mechanism should apply. Before composition, every candidate mechanism <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>
receives a scope</p>
<table id="S4.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau(m)\in\left\{\textsc{global}\right\}\cup\left\{\textsc{home}(d_{k})\right\}_{k=1}^{K}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">global</mtext><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>∪</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">home</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau(m)\in\left\{\textsc{global}\right\}\cup\left\{\textsc{home}(d_{k})\right\}_{k=1}^{K}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Writing <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{ev}(m)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ev</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{ev}(m)</annotation></semantics></math> for the items credited to <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>, the assignment follows one rule:</p>
<table id="S4.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau(m)=\begin{cases}\textsc{global}&amp;\text{if }\mathrm{ev}(m)\text{ meets two or more domains, or }m\text{ addresses a domain-independent failure mode,}\\
\textsc{home}(d_{k})&amp;\text{if }\mathrm{ev}(m)\subseteq D_{k}^{\mathrm{tr}}\text{ for exactly one }k,\\
\bot\ \text{(reject)}&amp;\text{if }\mathrm{ev}(m)\text{ is a single item.}\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">global</mtext></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext>if </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ev</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> meets two or more domains, or </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> addresses a domain-independent failure mode,</mtext></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">home</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mtext>if </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ev</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊆</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>tr</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> for exactly one </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mo rspace="0.722em">⊥</mo><mtext>(reject)</mtext></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mtext>if </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ev</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext> is a single item.</mtext></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau(m)=\begin{cases}\textsc{global}&amp;\text{if }\mathrm{ev}(m)\text{ meets two or more domains, or }m\text{ addresses a domain-independent failure mode,}\\
\textsc{home}(d_{k})&amp;\text{if }\mathrm{ev}(m)\subseteq D_{k}^{\mathrm{tr}}\text{ for exactly one }k,\\
\bot\ \text{(reject)}&amp;\text{if }\mathrm{ev}(m)\text{ is a single item.}\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Domain-independent failure modes are those the evidence cannot localize even in principle — malformed
output, execution failure, a generally applicable recovery procedure. A <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">global</span> mechanism enters as
one implementation applied to every input; a <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">home<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(d_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(d_{k})</annotation></semantics></math></span> mechanism enters conditionally, activated
only when the harness observes that the current input belongs to <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>; and the last case removes
adaptations that encode one problem’s quirk rather than a recurring class.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This distinction changes the structure of program conflicts. Suppose two clients modify the same behavior
in incompatible ways, but the evidence for each modification is confined to a different domain. A
parameter-space aggregator must either average the updates or choose one. EvolveNet can retain both
adaptations under disjoint domain conditions, so that many apparent conflicts become conditional
composition rather than a winner-take-all decision.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This property is not unconditional; what it requires can be stated exactly. Let <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa(x)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the
dispatch key the harness observes for input <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmproposition1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmproposition1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 1</span></span><span id="Thmproposition1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Scope isolation)<span id="Thmproposition1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmproposition1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmproposition1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmproposition1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> be adopted with scope <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textsc{home}(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">home</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textsc{home}(d)</annotation></semantics></math> and composed so that every statement it contributes is
reachable only under a guard testing <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa(x)=d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa(x)=d</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> writes no state read outside that guard and
alters no prompt text applied outside it, then for every input <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa(x)\neq d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa(x)\neq d</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(S\cup\{m\},\tau)(x)=h(S,\tau)(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>S</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(S\cup\{m\},\tau)(x)=h(S,\tau)(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="Thmproposition2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmproposition2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 2</span></span><span id="Thmproposition2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Conflicts under disjoint scopes)<span id="Thmproposition2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmproposition2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmproposition2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmproposition2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmproposition2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmproposition2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfy the hypothesis of Prop. <a href="#Thmproposition1" title="Proposition 1 (Scope isolation). ‣ Scope-typed composition. ‣ 4.3 Evidence-guided, scope-typed program aggregation ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> with scopes <math id="Thmproposition2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textsc{home}(d_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">home</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textsc{home}(d_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>
and <math id="Thmproposition2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\textsc{home}(d_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">home</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\textsc{home}(d_{j})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmproposition2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}\neq d_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>≠</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}\neq d_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math id="Thmproposition2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(S\cup\{m_{i},m_{j}\},\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(S\cup\{m_{i},m_{j}\},\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> agrees with
<math id="Thmproposition2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(S\cup\{m_{i}\},\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(S\cup\{m_{i}\},\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> on every input of domain <math id="Thmproposition2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and with <math id="Thmproposition2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(S\cup\{m_{j}\},\tau)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>∪</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>τ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(S\cup\{m_{j}\},\tau)</annotation></semantics></math> on every input of
domain <math id="Thmproposition2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>, whatever <math id="Thmproposition2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmproposition2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> do to the same behavior.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Both follow from the same observation: under the hypothesis the statements of a home-scoped
mechanism are unreachable off its domain and
no object read along that execution has been altered, so the two programs induce the same trace.
Prop. <a href="#Thmproposition2" title="Proposition 2 (Conflicts under disjoint scopes). ‣ Scope-typed composition. ‣ 4.3 Evidence-guided, scope-typed program aggregation ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> is what licenses the treatment of conflicts described above: two clients that
changed the same behavior in opposite directions need not be arbitrated at all if their evidence lies in
different domains, because each side is unreachable where the other applies. A parameter-space aggregator
has no counterpart of this move — coordinate-wise combination cannot make an update conditional on the
input it will later be asked about.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px4.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The value of these propositions lies in making the required isolation assumptions explicit rather than in
the proofs themselves. They state exactly what an implementation must respect for domain conditioning to
bound interference by construction, and they are why the aggregator introduces home-scoped material as
guarded extensions rather than as edits to shared prompt structure. Where the hypothesis fails — a mechanism that touches shared state despite its guard —
isolation does not hold, and the constraint of Eq. <a href="#S4.E12" title="In The adoption problem. ‣ 4.3 Evidence-guided, scope-typed program aggregation ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> is what detects it. Conflicts involving genuinely shared behavior, or mechanisms that interact through common state,
still require the aggregator to choose a single side. For a mechanism that is adopted under a home scope,
the server prefers preserving the client’s verified implementation rather than paraphrasing it, since
source-level rewriting may remove the behavior that produced the measured gain.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The adoption procedure.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Eq. <a href="#S4.E12" title="In The adoption problem. ‣ 4.3 Evidence-guided, scope-typed program aggregation ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> is approached in five steps. (i) Diff each
<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{k}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{k}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> against <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> to isolate what client <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> added. (ii) Read the execution traces attached to
that delta. (iii) Group the edits into mechanisms and attach to each the items of <math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{k}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{k}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> it is
credited with. (iv) Classify every mechanism by Eq. <a href="#S4.E14" title="In Scope-typed composition. ‣ 4.3 Evidence-guided, scope-typed program aggregation ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a>. (v) Compose: one implementation
per <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">global</span> mechanism, each <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">home<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(d)</annotation></semantics></math></span> mechanism copied verbatim into a branch guarded on
<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>, and conflicting mechanisms with disjoint home domains both retained — only <span id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">global</span>
conflicts are arbitrated, by graded evidence.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Steps (i)–(iii) are mechanical. Steps (iv) and (v) are carried out by an LLM merger applying the stated
criteria to the attached evidence, because deciding whether a mechanism’s evidence is localizable, and
how to place it without disturbing the base, requires reading the program rather than scoring it. That
division is what makes the operator testable: step (iv) is the only part the aggregation variants of
Sec. <a href="#S6.SS4" title="6.4 Is this aggregation, or routing in disguise? ‣ 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.4</span></a> change, so their differences are attributable to the classification rule
alone, and step (v)’s output is checked exactly against Eq. <a href="#S4.E12" title="In The adoption problem. ‣ 4.3 Evidence-guided, scope-typed program aggregation ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> before anything is
committed.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Preserving the shared base.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The shared harness is not treated as disposable source text. It
represents the behavioral state accumulated through previous rounds and therefore acts as a set of
load-bearing invariants during aggregation. This is particularly important for prompt rules: unlike a
conditional code path, an existing prompt instruction may influence every input. Rewriting or
“consolidating” such a rule can introduce system-wide changes unrelated to the mechanism being adopted.
Accordingly, the aggregator modifies the broadcast harness in place, preserves existing prompt rules, and
integrates new mechanisms as localized extensions whenever possible. The implementation also constrains
growth relative to the base harness; exact budget settings are reported with the experimental
configuration. These restrictions do not make composition risk-free, but they reduce the number of
unrelated behaviors changed by a single merge.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Behavioral commitment and rollback</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Program composition may introduce regressions that cannot be determined reliably from the source diffs
alone. EvolveNet therefore separates <em id="S4.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">construction</em> of a candidate shared harness from <em id="S4.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">commitment</em>
to that candidate. Let <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D^{\mathrm{val}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>D</mi><mi>val</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D^{\mathrm{val}}</annotation></semantics></math> be a validation slice that is disjoint from the client workloads
used to produce the candidate and from the final test set. Relative to the previous shared harness
<math id="S4.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>, define</p>
<table id="S4.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.E15"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle F_{\mathrm{val}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle F_{\mathrm{val}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E15.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle=\left\{i\in D^{\mathrm{val}}:v_{i}\!\left(h^{(t)}\right)=0,\,v_{i}\!\left(\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}\right)=1\right\}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mi>val</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\left\{i\in D^{\mathrm{val}}:v_{i}\!\left(h^{(t)}\right)=0,\,v_{i}\!\left(\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}\right)=1\right\},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S4.E16"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle B_{\mathrm{val}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle B_{\mathrm{val}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.E16.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle=\left\{i\in D^{\mathrm{val}}:v_{i}\!\left(h^{(t)}\right)=1,\,v_{i}\!\left(\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}\right)=0\right\}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mi>val</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>}</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\left\{i\in D^{\mathrm{val}}:v_{i}\!\left(h^{(t)}\right)=1,\,v_{i}\!\left(\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}\right)=0\right\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(16)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">The candidate is committed iff</p>
<table id="S4.E17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|F_{\mathrm{val}}\right|\geq\left|B_{\mathrm{val}}\right|." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|F_{\mathrm{val}}\right|\geq\left|B_{\mathrm{val}}\right|.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.3" class="ltx_p">The gate compares behavioral transitions item by item rather than subtracting aggregate scores. Most items
are unchanged between two related harnesses; focusing on the items that flip makes the decision depend on
the behavioral difference introduced by the merge.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">When the candidate fails the test, the aggregator receives the observed regressions and is allowed one
revision. If the revised candidate also fails, the round rolls back to <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>. Rollback always targets
the previous shared harness, not the best-performing client, preserving the invariant that every round
begins from one shared program state. The gate protects the committed validation trajectory under the
criterion in Eq. <a href="#S4.E17" title="In 4.4 Behavioral commitment and rollback ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a>; it does not guarantee improvement on an unseen test
distribution. Its role is narrower: to prevent an aggregation whose measured regressions outnumber its
measured gains from becoming the shared starting point of all subsequent local searches. Because the test consumes only per-item verdicts, it can also be computed without centralizing
validation items: with the slice partitioned across clients, each returns two integers and the server sums
them, reproducing the same accept/reject decision. The revision step is different — it shows the
aggregator which items regressed — so the two-integer variant supports gating but not revision.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.5 </span>The complete EvolveNet procedure</h3>

<figure id="alg1" class="ltx_float ltx_float_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float"><span id="alg1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm 1</span> </span> EvolveNet: one communication round</figcaption>
<div id="alg1.4" class="ltx_listing ltx_listing">
<div id="alg1.l1" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">1:</span>
              
              
             <span id="alg1.l1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">input:</span> shared harness <math id="alg1.l1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>; client workloads <math id="alg1.l1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="D_{1:K}^{\mathrm{tr}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>tr</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{1:K}^{\mathrm{tr}}</annotation></semantics></math>; validation
slice <math id="alg1.l1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D^{\mathrm{val}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>D</mi><mi>val</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D^{\mathrm{val}}</annotation></semantics></math>; local search budget <math id="alg1.l1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(E,G)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>E</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>G</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(E,G)</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l2" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">2:</span>
              
              
             <span id="alg1.l2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span> <math id="alg1.l2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=1</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">to</span> <math id="alg1.l2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">in parallel</span> <span id="alg1.l2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">do</span>



</div>
<div id="alg1.l3" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">3:</span>
              
              
              <math id="alg1.l3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{k}^{(t)}\leftarrow\textsc{LocalEvolve}\left(h^{(t)},D_{k}^{\mathrm{tr}},E,G\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">LocalEvolve</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>tr</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi>E</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{k}^{(t)}\leftarrow\textsc{LocalEvolve}\left(h^{(t)},D_{k}^{\mathrm{tr}},E,G\right)</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l4" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">4:</span>
              
              
              <math id="alg1.l4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{k}^{(t)}\leftarrow\operatorname{diff}\left(h^{(t)},h_{k}^{(t)}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mi>diff</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{k}^{(t)}\leftarrow\operatorname{diff}\left(h^{(t)},h_{k}^{(t)}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l5" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">5:</span>
              
              
              <math id="alg1.l5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{k}^{(t)}\leftarrow\textsc{BehaviorChanges}\left(h_{k}^{(t)},h^{(t)};D_{k}^{\mathrm{tr}}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">BehaviorChanges</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>tr</mi></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{k}^{(t)}\leftarrow\textsc{BehaviorChanges}\left(h_{k}^{(t)},h^{(t)};D_{k}^{\mathrm{tr}}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l6" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">6:</span>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l7" class="ltx_listingline">

             <math id="alg1.l7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}\leftarrow\textsc{ScopeAggregate}\left(h^{(t)},\left\{\left(\Delta_{k}^{(t)},e_{k}^{(t)}\right)\right\}_{k=1}^{K}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">ScopeAggregate</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}\leftarrow\textsc{ScopeAggregate}\left(h^{(t)},\left\{\left(\Delta_{k}^{(t)},e_{k}^{(t)}\right)\right\}_{k=1}^{K}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l8" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">8:</span>
              
              
             <math id="alg1.l8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(F_{\mathrm{val}},B_{\mathrm{val}})\leftarrow\textsc{Compare}\left(\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)},h^{(t)};D^{\mathrm{val}}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Compare</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>D</mi><mi>val</mi></msup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(F_{\mathrm{val}},B_{\mathrm{val}})\leftarrow\textsc{Compare}\left(\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)},h^{(t)};D^{\mathrm{val}}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l9" class="ltx_listingline">

             <span id="alg1.l9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">if</span> <math id="alg1.l9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|B_{\mathrm{val}}|&gt;|F_{\mathrm{val}}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|B_{\mathrm{val}}|&gt;|F_{\mathrm{val}}|</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">then</span>



</div>
<div id="alg1.l10" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">10:</span>
              
              
              <math id="alg1.l10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}\leftarrow\textsc{ReviseAggregate}\left(h^{(t)},\left\{\left(\Delta_{k}^{(t)},e_{k}^{(t)}\right)\right\}_{k=1}^{K},B_{\mathrm{val}}\right)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">ReviseAggregate</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo>{</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>e</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}\leftarrow\textsc{ReviseAggregate}\left(h^{(t)},\left\{\left(\Delta_{k}^{(t)},e_{k}^{(t)}\right)\right\}_{k=1}^{K},B_{\mathrm{val}}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l11" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">11:</span>
              
              
              recompute <math id="alg1.l11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(F_{\mathrm{val}},B_{\mathrm{val}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(F_{\mathrm{val}},B_{\mathrm{val}})</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l12" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">12:</span>
              
              
             <span id="alg1.l12.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">end</span> <span id="alg1.l12.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">if</span>
</div>
<div id="alg1.l13" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">13:</span>
              
              
             <math id="alg1.l13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(t+1)}\leftarrow\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(t+1)}\leftarrow\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l13.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">if</span> <math id="alg1.l13.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|F_{\mathrm{val}}|\geq|B_{\mathrm{val}}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>val</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|F_{\mathrm{val}}|\geq|B_{\mathrm{val}}|</annotation></semantics></math>
<span id="alg1.l13.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">else</span> <math id="alg1.l13.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l14" class="ltx_listingline">
              <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline">14:</span>
              
              
             <span id="alg1.l14.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">return</span> <math id="alg1.l14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(t+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(t+1)}</annotation></semantics></math>

</div>
</div>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ 4.5 The complete EvolveNet procedure ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> states one round. The server broadcasts <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> to all <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> clients. Each client
independently evolves it on its local workload and returns a specialist harness <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{k}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{k}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>, its
common-base delta, and its behavioral evidence. The server decomposes the deltas into candidate
mechanisms, assigns each a global or home-domain scope, and composes them into <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>h</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{h}^{(t+1)}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The candidate is compared with <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D^{\mathrm{val}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>D</mi><mi>val</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D^{\mathrm{val}}</annotation></semantics></math> and committed only if it passes
Eq. <a href="#S4.E17" title="In 4.4 Behavioral commitment and rollback ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a>; otherwise it is revised once and, if still unsuccessful, discarded.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Experimental Setup</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate EvolveNet on five settings with a natural axis of agent specialization; each unit of
specialization is one data-local client in the protocol. Clients are databases on BIRD
text-to-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al. 2023</a>)</cite>, libraries on DS-1000 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lai et al. 2023</a>)</cite>, repositories on SWE-bench
Verified <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jimenez et al. 2024</a>)</cite>, task families on ClawEval (agentic workflow tasks over an OpenClaw
agent with mock enterprise services), and difficulty bands on LiveCodeBench
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jain et al. 2025</a>)</cite>, which serves as a smaller robustness check since its single-platform pool
admits no five-way sharding. Weights <math id="S5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> in the accessible client mixture <math id="S5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{client}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒫</mi><mi>client</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{client}}</annotation></semantics></math> are uniform, and each client’s proposer is given a
search role — conservative repair, independent exploration, or adversarial audit — assigned by client
index so that concurrent branches do not collapse onto the same edit; Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Prompts ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>
reproduces the specialist instruction and the aggregator’s adoption rule verbatim. We use <math id="S5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}5</annotation></semantics></math> clients everywhere
except LiveCodeBench (<math id="S5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}3</annotation></semantics></math>), and
<math id="S5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T{=}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T{=}3</annotation></semantics></math> rounds throughout, with one local generation and one proposer branch per round
(<math id="S5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E{=}G{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E{=}G{=}1</annotation></semantics></math> in Alg. <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ 4.5 The complete EvolveNet procedure ‣ 4 Method: EvolveNet ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). Held-out sets contain 150 (BIRD), 200 (DS-1000), 40 (SWE-bench) and
30 items (ClawEval, LiveCodeBench); splits are fixed with seed 0 and every item passed a gold check
in our environment before use (Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Benchmark Construction and Gold Auditing ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>). Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Shards and Splits ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> gives the per-client shards and split sizes.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The frozen solver is deepseek-v4-flash throughout, and the same model drives the client proposers and
the server’s aggregator; Sec. <a href="#S6.SS7" title="6.7 Does any of this depend on the model? ‣ 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.7</span></a> repeats the pipeline with a different stack. Only
the harness adapts: a static auditor rejects any candidate that changes the model, endpoint, or
credentials, or that reads a gold answer at inference. Labels enter the loop at two points only — clients
select candidates on their own shard, the server gates merges on its validation slice — and test sets
are evaluated after the shared harness is frozen. BIRD served as the development benchmark, on which the
aggregation operator, the gate, and the loop design were selected; the operator was then frozen and the
remaining four settings were each run end-to-end once. DS-1000 was designated in advance as the primary
confirmation benchmark, being the setting whose clients hold the most disjoint workloads. Solver replies
are cached on the full request and every child process runs with a pinned hash seed, so that a score
difference between two harnesses reflects a behavioral difference rather than sampling noise
(Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Measurement Details ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Results</h2>

<section id="S6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.1 </span>How much does a run vary?</h3>

<div id="S6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Every comparison below is calibrated against this measurement, which we therefore establish first. We have three
independent executions of the identical BIRD round-0 protocol (same shards, same specialist instruction,
same budget; only sampling differs). Client-level validation scores vary by 2–4 items across
these runs: the same mixed-shard client scores 66% and 69% on the validation slice in two
runs, the formula_1 specialist 62% and 66%, the toxicology specialist 62% and
65%; whole clients oscillate between returning an evolved program and returning the broadcast
unchanged. Held-out scores of end-to-end finals produced by the same rule vary comparably (e.g. the
select-best final scores 66.7% and 69.3% across two independent runs).</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This spread sets the resolution of every comparison that follows. Differences of a few items fall inside
it, so harnesses cannot be ranked by their totals. For each realized pair of harnesses we therefore
report paired per-item outcomes rather than relying on aggregate score differences: the unit of evidence
is a behavioral flip on a specific problem, not a shift in a sum.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The same spread separates the two roles a validation slice can play. As a gate it is sound: an accept or
reject decision turns on which items flip, and flips are visible above the noise. As a ranking signal it
is not — on DS-1000 the client with the highest validation total is nine points worse on held-out data
than a merged harness with a lower one (Sec. <a href="#S6.SS3" title="6.3 Validation score does not rank programs — which is why the gate only gates ‣ 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.3</span></a>). EvolveNet reads the slice only for per-item
decisions, never to declare a winner.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.2 </span>Main results</h3>

<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S6.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 6.2 Main results ‣ 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> reports the held-out accuracy of the shared harness after <math id="S6.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> EvolveNet rounds,
against the unevolved harness from which every client starts.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 1: </span>Held-out accuracy (%) of the shared harness before evolution and after <math id="S6.T1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> EvolveNet
rounds — whether experience extracted locally and aggregated as program adaptations becomes cumulative
improvement in the common starting program. ClawEval is graded on a continuous scale, so its column reports the mean
task score.</figcaption>

<td id="S6.T1.2.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S6.T1.2.3.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">70.7</span></td>
<td id="S6.T1.2.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S6.T1.2.3.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">68.5</span></td>
<td id="S6.T1.2.3.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S6.T1.2.3.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">66.7</span></td>
<td id="S6.T1.2.3.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S6.T1.2.3.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">57.5</span></td>
<td id="S6.T1.2.3.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb"><span id="S6.T1.2.3.6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">74.1</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Collaborative evolution improves the shared harness on every setting, by 13.4 points on BIRD,
13.0 on DS-1000, 33.4 on LiveCodeBench, 20.0 on SWE-bench and 8.3 on ClawEval.
Each improvement is significant under a paired test on that benchmark’s held-out set — an exact McNemar
test on binary outcomes, and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test on ClawEval’s continuous judge scores — with
<math id="S6.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> of 5.4e-4 (BIRD, win 26 / lose 6), 6.2e-6 (DS-1000, win 30 / lose
4), 2.0e-3 (LiveCodeBench, win 10 / lose 0), 0.021 (SWE-bench, win 9 /
lose 1) and 0.022 (ClawEval, better 18 / worse 7); all five survive Holm correction
for the five comparisons. EvolveNet also improves on retaining the strongest single client in all five settings
(Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Keeping the Strongest Client, Across All Five Settings ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>), by margins that widen as the clients’ workloads diverge — from
1.4 points on BIRD, whose eleven databases share one task shape, to 23.4 on LiveCodeBench.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Two properties of the trajectory are worth noting. The gain is not delivered in one step
(Fig. <a href="#S6.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 6.2 Main results ‣ 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>): on DS-1000 the merged program goes from 60.0% after one round to
68.5% after three, with items broken by one round’s merge recovered by the next, and on
LiveCodeBench and SWE-bench the final round adds a further 16.7 and 17.5 points on held-out
data over the artifact that preceded it. Nor is it confined to the libraries clients trained on: on DS-1000 the merged harness improves over the
unevolved harness on every library (Table <a href="#S6.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 6.2 Main results ‣ 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>), including one that no client trained on. The remainder of this section asks what the aggregation operator contributes to these numbers
(Sec. <a href="#S6.SS4" title="6.4 Is this aggregation, or routing in disguise? ‣ 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.4</span></a>), whether the adaptations clients discover are actually retained
(Sec. <a href="#S6.SS5" title="6.5 Does experience accumulate across agents? ‣ 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.5</span></a>), and what the merged programs contain (Sec. <a href="#S6.SS9" title="6.9 What the aggregator actually does ‣ 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.9</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T2" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2: </span>DS-1000 held-out accuracy by library (%). <em id="S6.T2.8" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Delegation</em>, <em id="S6.T2.9" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">GLOBAL-only</em> and
<em id="S6.T2.10" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">EvolveNet</em> are built from one identical final-round client snapshot; <em id="S6.T2.11" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">select-best</em> is the

The gate keeps the committed trajectory non-decreasing — a rejected
merge leaves the curve flat rather than falling — provided the slice is fixed and scoring is
deterministic (Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Measurement Details ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>). Scores are percentages of the slice maximum; ClawEval’s is

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span>BIRD accuracy against how much faster an EvolveNet round completes than the same local searches executed
serially, counting the non-parallelizable aggregation and gating steps; the client phase alone parallelizes
1.9–5.4<math id="S6.F3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> (Sec. <a href="#S6.SS8" title="6.8 Scaling evolutionary search through parallel trajectories ‣ 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.8</span></a>). Splitting a fixed workload buys wall-clock without
costing accuracy: every multi-client configuration is at or above <math id="S6.F3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}1</annotation></semantics></math>. The decline at <math id="S6.F3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K{=}7" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K{=}7</annotation></semantics></math> is a
shard-size effect: splitting the mixed shard by database leaves its three sub-clients with only 6–8 items
each, and their candidates overfit them.</figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.3 </span>Validation score does not rank programs — which is why the gate only gates</h3>

<div id="S6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The server’s validation slice is essential for gating and selection, but it cannot be used to
<em id="S6.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">conclude</em>. On DS-1000 the select-best client scored 69% on validation but 59.5% on
test, while the merged harness scored 63% on validation and 68.5% on test. Ranking by validation would
invert the true ordering — consistent with the variance measurement of Sec. <a href="#S6.SS1" title="6.1 How much does a run vary? ‣ 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6.1</span></a>. EvolveNet
therefore uses validation only for per-item accept/reject decisions (which are robust: they compare
behavior flips, not totals), and all conclusions in this paper are drawn from held-out test sets with
paired significance tests.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.4 </span>Is this aggregation, or routing in disguise?</h3>

<div id="S6.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A scope-typed merge contains domain-conditioned material, which invites an alternative explanation: that
EvolveNet simply preserves <math id="S6.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> specialists and dispatches by domain, and that no genuine composition occurs.
We test this on DS-1000, the setting whose clients hold the most disjoint workloads, by replaying
alternative aggregators on the <em id="S6.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">same</em> final-round client snapshot (Table <a href="#S6.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 6.4 Is this aggregation, or routing in disguise? ‣ 6 Results ‣ EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>). The most
important comparison is against <em id="S6.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">select-best</em>, which performs no aggregation at all and simply keeps
whichever client scores highest on the server’s validation slice — the obvious thing to do if program
composition were unnecessary.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span>Do the two halves of the operator each earn their place? <em id="S6.T3.8" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Delegation</em>, <em id="S6.T3.9" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">GLOBAL-only</em>
and <em id="S6.T3.10" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">EvolveNet</em> are built from one identical snapshot of DS-1000 client harnesses and evaluated on the
same held-out set, so differences among them are attributable to the aggregation rule alone;
<em id="S6.T3.11" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">select-best</em> is the end-to-end baseline protocol, a run in which the server promotes the
strongest client instead of aggregating. <em id="S6.T3.12" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Delegation</em> performs no composition at all: it keeps all
<math id="S6.T3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> client programs and dispatches each item to its library’s owner. <em id="S6.T3.13" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">GLOBAL-only</em> is EvolveNet with
domain conditioning forbidden — the aggregator may promote a mechanism only on cross-library evidence.</figcaption>
<table id="S6.T3.14" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S6.T3.14.1" class="ltx_tr">

<th id="S6.T3.14.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">Composition</th>
<th id="S6.T3.14.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">Domain gating</th>
<th id="S6.T3.14.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">Held-out (%)</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">

<td id="S6.T3.14.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t">—</td>
<td id="S6.T3.14.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t">—</td>
<td id="S6.T3.14.2.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t">55.5</td></tr>
<tr id="S6.T3.14.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S6.T3.14.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left">Select-best client (no aggregation)</td>
<td id="S6.T3.14.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">—</td>
<td id="S6.T3.14.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">—</td>
<td id="S6.T3.14.3.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">59.5</td></tr>
<tr id="S6.T3.14.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="S6.T3.14.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left">Delegation (keep <math id="S6.T3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> programs, dispatch)</td>
<td id="S6.T3.14.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">no</td>
<td id="S6.T3.14.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">yes</td>
<td id="S6.T3.14.4.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">64.0</td></tr>
